newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel cuts rate 0.3 point to 15.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel cuts rate 0.3 point to 15.2 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for November by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 15.2 percent.
The rate is the one charged commercial banks at daily and weekly monetary tenders.
The central bank said that since August it had lowered its short-term base rate by 1.8 percentage points. Last month the central bank also lowered the interest rate by 0.3 percentage point.
Israel's financial markets had been predicting that the central bank would lower interest rates by up to 0.5 percentage point.
A central bank spokesman said the decision was influenced by mixed indicators.
On the one hand the rise in consumer prices has been low in the past few months and M1 money supply has expanded at a rate consistent with economic activity.

On the other hand inflation is still running above the government's 1996 target of 8-10 percent and inflationary expectations in the capital market, while stable, are also above the government's target.
The market's expectation for inflation in the coming 12 months is 11.25 percent.
